arguments.summary: A credential compromise on workstation WS-FIN-042 (user jsmith) led to the execution of a Cobalt Strike beacon via a phishing email. The attacker used encoded PowerShell to download and execute an unsigned DLL from the user's Temp directory, establishing command-and-control (C2) communication with a known malicious IP (198.51.100.23) and a fallback domain (c2.update-service.xyz). Lateral movement was attempted via SMB to a file server. The threat was contained by revoking the user's credentials, blocking C2 infrastructure at the firewall, and remediating the host with a full EPP scan and automated hardening playbook.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dropper {
    meta:
        description = "Detects common Cobalt Strike beacon dropper patterns in PowerShell scripts"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        date = "2026-04-11"
        hash = "a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2"
    strings:
        $powershell_decode = /-enc(oded)?command/ nocase
        $temp_path = /\\AppData\\(Local|Roaming)\\Temp\\/ nocase
        $dll_load = /rundll32.*\\Temp\\.*\.dll/ nocase
        $beacon_mutex = "Global\\MSCTF.Asm.{b1e5}"
    condition:
        $powershell_decode and $temp_path and $dll_load and $beacon_mutex
}
